the children in the study were able to teach and learn machine learning with the help of the Teachable Machine, and that they were able to reason about the connection between their bodily expressions and the ML tool's responses.
the young children were able to teach and learn about machine learning, and that they were able to do so in a way that was consistent with sociocultural theories of participation.
very young children can learn machine learning and that they can teach it to others.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions: How do very young children participate in machine learning?
how children learn about machine learning in nonschool settings and how children can teach and explore the world through their own embodied interaction with machine learning.
how children learn and teach with machine learning.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

children are able to teach machine learning systems, and in the process they learn about the relationship between themselves and machine learning systems, as well as how to interact with machine learning systems.
the results from this case study illustrate that children can teach themselves machine learning and that this is a promising direction to pursue in the future.
children can learn and teach machine learning in a very short time, and that the learning process is highly interactive, embodied and situated.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
children's participation in machine learning can be seen as an embodied, multimodal and collaborative process where the children are actively engaged in the process of teaching and exploring.
the children were teaching each other and themselves about machine learning and that the process of learning was highly social and embodied.
children can learn machine learning and that machine learning can be learned in a playful and embodied way.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the children's own agency and participation in machine learning activities is crucial for them to understand the affordances of machine learning systems as well as for them to be able to make sense of their own role as learners.

the process of teaching and exploring machine learning with very small children is a social and cultural process that can support the development of children's agency in the context of machine learning.
machine learning and AI should be taught to young children in ways that are not only playful, but also in ways that support their participation in the design of machine learning systems.
